question: Why do loop and dream structures assert the 26 world edges that never entered a served window, starting from the carriers' candidate formation?
definition: A per-edge replay trace of the 26 rows in docs/assertion_provenance.json. For each row it records every final loop/dream path that contains the edge, the first cycle that carrier appeared, the loop/dream evidence, the final temporal counts in both directions, and whether a prediction candidate is a final source.
method: Same six Q4 seeds, 120 cycles, cap 40 and acquisition schedule as the provenance replay. The replay refuses to write unless each seed reproduces the stored asserted-world fingerprint and edge count. Candidate formation cycles are read from the sleep reports; final carriers are deduplicated by candidate id. No seed, arm, cap or engine edit is added.

findings: All 26 direct edges are present in the final temporal graph at count 23-47, above PREDICTION_MIN_COUNT=5; the direct edge is not a floor miss.

Every row has a loop carrier: 61 loop-candidate occurrences, of which 58 are 3-cycles and 3 are 2-cycles. Every loop path contains the pair, and structure_edges expands each path edge in both directions.
The loop builder requires a minimum edge count of 5 and consumes temporal cycles, not served windows; the first observed carrier formations span cycles 37-117.
18 rows have the reverse orientation served and 8 have neither orientation served; both kinds still have a loop path containing the pair, which is why the loop readout supplies the direct assertion.
One row has a dream co-carrier as well; no row is carried only by a dream, and no row has a prediction candidate as its final assertion source.

not_evidence: A replay-only carrier trace on six committed Q4 seeds, one world family, one build and one cap. It explains how loop/dream paths reach the readout; it does not show that serving the direct edge would change A_W, does not decompose the full prediction-ranking history, and does not establish capability, retention, transfer or a general engine property.
